Claire (Design): Quick design question — we've got a token-usage heatmap in dark mode that looks nice but some colors are almost indistinguishable for a11y. Thoughts on switching to a colorblind-safe spectrum? :thinking:
Jamal (Eng-UI): agree, current red->purple is pretty but fails colorblind checks. Maybe use a sequential blue->orange with luminance steps?
Rachel (PM): Users care most about 'hot' vs 'cold' buckets, not exact hue. As long as contrast and tooltip labels are clear we're fine. Can we add patterned fills for the densest buckets for extra redundancy?
Tom (Eng-ML): Patterned fills might be noisy at small sizes. What if we add a high-contrast toggle that swaps the heatmap to a mono-chromatic gradient + strong border?
Anika (Accessibility): Prefer having both: colorblind-safe palette by default + optional "High contrast" toggle. Also add aria labels for each cell and make the legend keyboard-focusable. WCAG contrast target: 4.5:1 for text/icons. Heatmap cells should have clear hover outlines for focus.
Jamal (Eng-UI): Good call. Proposed palette I tested quickly: `#08306b -> #2171b5 -> #6baed6 -> #fdae6b -> #ef3b2c` — perceptually ordered, passes deutan/protan simulators in my quick run.
Claire (Design): Can you paste the simulator screenshots here? Also thinking about syntax highlighting in logs panel — our dark code background is `#0b1220` and tokens are low-contrast. Need better token colors for keywords/strings.
Jamal (Eng-UI): Pasted sim: https://figma.internal/redwood/design/token-heatmap-cb-sims (internal). For code, I propose these token colors on dark bg `#0b1220`: keyword `#9ad2ff`, string `#ffd29f`, number `#ffd86b`, comment `#6b7683`. Comments are intentionally muted.
Anika (Accessibility): Ensure keyword and string meet contrast against `#0b1220`. `#9ad2ff` -> contrast 7.0:1, `#ffd29f` -> 5.1:1, both OK. Comments at `#6b7683` are below 4.5:1 — that's fine if considered decorative, but must be perceivable when focused. Consider `prefers-reduced-motion` and high-contrast media queries for chart animations.
Rachel (PM): Small UX copy tweak: in theme dropdown replace "Dark (default)" with "Dark — production-friendly"? Might be overzealous but helps set expectations for contrast.
Claire (Design): I like shorter: "Dark (high contrast)" vs "Dark (balanced)" — tests later. Also need copy for the accessibility toggle — current label "High contrast" or "Enhanced contrast"?
Anika (Accessibility): Use "Enhanced contrast" — clearer semantics. Add a help tooltip: "Increases color contrast and adds high-visibility outlines".
Tom (Eng-ML): Minor perf note: switching heatmap patterns adds SVG elements; we should batch updates. I'll coordinate with Jamal on render paths.
Jamal (Eng-UI): Will implement CSS variables so theme changes are instant. Example snippet for the heatmap vars:
```css
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --heat-1: #08306b;
  --heat-2: #2171b5;
  --heat-3: #6baed6;
  --heat-4: #fdae6b;
  --heat-5: #ef3b2c;
}
:root[data-theme="dark"][data-contrast="high"] {
  --heat-1: #051033;
  --heat-5: #b30000; /* stronger hot */
}
```
Claire (Design): Nice. Can we also standardize chart tooltip shadows — they're almost invisible in dark mode. Use `rgba(0,0,0,0.6)` over a light blur?
Jamal (Eng-UI): Tooltip in dark should be `background: rgba(11,18,32,0.9); box-shadow: 0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,0.7);` — I'll add to tokens.
Rachel (PM): Next steps: Jamal to push a dev build with palette + high-contrast toggle, Anika to run an accessibility audit, Claire to update figma tokens and small copy change for dropdown. Tom to verify perf. Target: staging by end of sprint. :rocket:
theme-bot: Automated test run queued — color-contrast-checker v2.1 started for branch `design/heatmap-a11y`.
Jamal (Eng-UI): Thanks all — I'll open a PR and link the staging preview here.
Claire (Design): Thanks! I'll add a micro-usability test for the legend interpretation.
Anika (Accessibility): Ping me when PR's up, I'll run axe + keyboard tests. :white_check_mark:
